title: Fanout pacing shim to stabilize tokens/sec during mixed-variant bursts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Customer reports and automated alerts observed a sudden, repeatable drop in tokens/sec and increased TTFT for multi-variant fanouts across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. First-byte latency for affected requests rose from a median of ~120ms to ~560ms on impacted worker pools; tokens/sec throughput dropped ~55-70% for several 70B/30B mixed workloads.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- The route splitter began issuing concurrent priming/initial requests to multiple variant kernels for the same logical model simultaneously.
- This parallel fanout produced a spike in KV cache churn and caused repeated kernel selection churn on heterogeneous GPU nodes (mix of A100 and H100 variants and int8 quantized paths).
- Kernel scheduling and small-sample sequence patterns triggered a slow path in the runtime that serialized early token generation for multiplexed streams.
- Combined with per-tenant burst allowances, several tenants exhausted warmup credits and bumped into inflated coldstart windows, amplifying TTFT regressions.

Mitigation applied (hotfix):
- Implemented a lightweight "pacing shim" in the router that limits simultaneous variant fanout per request to a configurable burst_budget (default 2) and introduces a short randomized jitter window to avoid synchronized warmups.
- Added a per-request header X-RDW-PACING to surface decisions to downstream workers for debugging.
- Introduced a temporary soft-degrade path that forces single-variant execution for tenants exceeding warmup credit thresholds.
- Deployed a circuit-breaker to detect repeated KV miss storms and fall back to cached-compatible variant immediately.

Deployment plan and rollout: 
- Canary (region us-west-2, 5% traffic) rolled at 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC. Monitoring dashboards showed TTFT return to baseline within 6 minutes for canary shard.
- Staged ramp to 25% (hosted) and selective Dedicated pools with identical kernel mix on 2026-03-12. Private customers were contacted with opt-in toggle (remote config) due to potential networking constraints.
- Full rollout target: 2026-03-18 after validation and pairwise regression tests.

Workaround for customers (if needed):
- Advise temporarily pinning traffic to a single verified variant in model catalog (older but warm) or increasing reserved warmup credits for Dedicated.
- For Private deployments, operators can enable router flag redwood.pacing.force_single_variant via control-plane until full patch is accepted.

Monitoring and validation:
- New dashboard: "fanout-pacing/ttft-tokenssec" added to Console under Serving Reliability. Alerts threshold: first-byte latency > 300ms sustained for 2m and tokens/sec drop >40% relative to 1h baseline.
- Synthetic harness updated to include mixed-variant stress tests (70B-int8 + 30B-fp16 priming patterns).

Next steps / follow-ups:
- Engineering: refine burst_budget heuristic with per-tenant historical warmup telemetry and implement adaptive reservoir instead of static cap.
- Research: replay traces to quantify root regression trigger and evaluate kernel selection backoff strategies.
- Product/Support: update incident notes for customers and add a KB article describing pacing behavior and recommended configurations.
- Release: merge hotfix into runtime-1.24.0 branch and schedule post-mortem in Cycle 2026-W11.
